name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 19 points in Chicago
Quigley holds about $1.1 million on hand; Hanson reports no fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent
No polls or outside spending signal any competitive threat
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same direction: a D+19 district, a long-tenured incumbent with a seven-figure war chest, a challenger with no reported finances, and markets pricing a Democratic win at 96 percent. With no polls or expert ratings to complicate the picture, the expected margin stays near 25 points.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for Hanson or an unexpected scandal involving Quigley could narrow the margin, though an upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Illinois's 5th District, anchored on Chicago's North Side, leans Democratic by about 19 points, and Mike Quigley has held the seat since 2009. He enters the general election with roughly $1.1 million on hand after raising nearly $1 million, while Republican Tommy Hanson shows no reported fundraising or cash reserves. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, candidate finances, and betting markets, which price Quigley's chances near 96 percent.

With no polling to weigh and no outside spending targeting the incumbent, the expected margin sits near 25 points. Quigley's incumbency and the district's partisan makeup make an upset highly unlikely; the main uncertainty is turnout in a low-profile contest rather than the outcome itself.
